question: Do the CPU capture's callback totals use the same units and aggregation as the ordinary timing batch, and can their magnitudes be compared?
answer: The raw callback totals use the same millisecond units and runner aggregation, but the single profiled invocation is not a timing reproduction attempt. Debugger and CPU Profiler instrumentation, one fixed-order observation per slot, and different batch quantity/order prevent quantitative comparison with the ordinary eight-run medians or fresh twelve-run table batch.

unitsAndAggregation.rawTotalDefinition: results.sync + results.timeout + results.animation_frame + results.microtask + results.promise after the boot snapshot and reset
unitsAndAggregation.cpuCaptureStorage: One unrounded window.runBenchmark result object per slot is stored directly in the CPU receipt.
unitsAndAggregation.ordinaryStorage: The unchanged driver prints every per-run total rounded to 0.1 ms, reports the median of eight raw totals rounded to 0.1 ms, and reports each bucket's median independently.
unitsAndAggregation.ordinaryParser: The parser verifies 32 rounded samples, cyclic order, exact representative callback counts, and agreement between each reported total median and the eight rounded samples within 0.100001 ms.
unitsAndAggregation.bucketMedianWarning: Independently reported ordinary bucket medians cannot be summed to reconstruct the total median. Preview optimized sync 56.9 plus animation-frame 250.6 equals 307.5, while the independently computed total median is 308.1.

freshTwelveRunTableControl.note: This ordinary unprofiled batch uses duplicate byte-identical published-preview baselines and confirms that the profiled 71/82 ms level is not representative ordinary timing. It does not establish why the profile invocation differs.

protocolEqualities: Exact runner.html, run.mjs and server.mjs bytes
Same frozen harness and served application assets
Item count 100 and the same add, toggle and delete workload
Same boot settle, boot snapshot and measurement reset
Exactly 400 synchronous and 400 animation-frame callbacks with all other callback buckets zero
Same CSS interception and final DOM expectations
Fresh browser context for each workload
Iframe size 800 by 600 and default Playwright context viewport; neither path sets a viewport override
Headless Chromium 153.0.8010.12 with no explicit custom browser arguments
protocolDifferences: The CPU invocation enables Debugger and CPU Profiler, sets a 100 microsecond sampling interval, and starts profiling before iframe boot; ordinary timing enables neither.
The CPU invocation retains one fixed-order observation per slot: optimized main, optimized preview, naive main, naive preview.
The ordinary batch retains eight observations per slot, 32 total, in cyclic order with each slot visiting every ordinal position twice, then reports medians.
Both reuse one browser process with fresh contexts, but the ordinary browser spans 32 workloads while the CPU browser spans four.
Neither timing driver declares an explicit warmup. The ordinary batch has repeated browser-process observations per slot; the CPU invocation has one.
The ordinary run had separate semantic preflights before timing. The CPU capture performs hash and semantic guards inside its own invocation but does not run the ordinary preflight program.
The CPU profile span is boot-inclusive, although its runner callback total excludes boot after the same reset. Ordinary timing retains only the post-reset callback total.

The CPU receipt authenticates the Chromium executable SHA-256. The ordinary log authenticates Chromium version 153.0.8010.12, but its execution receipt does not store the executable hash. Both load Playwright from the frozen driver installation.
interpretation: The exact 71.020 and 82.505 ms totals and their 11.485 ms difference are valid values observed under the single instrumented invocation.
They are not a reproduction attempt and must not be compared quantitatively with the ordinary 207.4 and 308.1 ms medians.
The 19.268 ms difference in source-mapped app-bundle self samples likewise cannot allocate or explain the ordinary 100.7 ms difference.
The profiles remain useful for reached-work counts and descriptive source attribution under their instrumented, boot-inclusive sampling window.
The magnitude mismatch neither proves sampling or idle time is the stronger explanation nor rules out a future bounded Chrome lifecycle trace.
